question.value: Improve the rotation-tunneling line list, constrain the excitation temperature, and confirm 3-hydroxypropenal toward IRAS16293 B.

evidence.quote: We want to extend the existing rotational line list of 3-hydroxypropenal to shed more light on the recent observational results and to facilitate additional radio astronomical searches for this molecule.
Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) models were carried out and compared to the observations to constrain the excitation temperature.
Additional transitions were searched for in other ALMA archival data of the same source to confirm the presence of 3-hydroxypropenal.

method.value: Assign laboratory rotation-tunneling lines iteratively; fit spectroscopic parameters with SPFIT and calculate spectra with SPCAT.

evidence.quote: Pickett’s programs SPCAT and SPFIT (cite: spfit_1991) were used to calculate and fit the rotational spectra of 3-hydroxypropenal.
We tested after each round of assignments if one or more spectroscopic parameters would improve the quality of the fit by amounts that warranted keeping the respective parameter in the fit.
The measurements between 150 and 330 GHz and between 400 and 660 GHz were carried out with the Lille spectrometer (cite: Lille-spectrometer).

key_parameters.value: Final present-study list: 11551 transitions at 7551 different frequencies; J ≤ 100, Ka ≤ 59, Kc ≤ 97.

evidence.quote: Our final line list consisted of 11551 transitions from the present study which correspond to 7551 different frequencies, mostly because of unresolved asymmetry splitting.
The quantum numbers $J$, $K_a$, and $K_c$ reach values of 100, 59, and 97.

assumptions.value: Watson’s S reduced Hamiltonian in the prolate Ir representation on the diagonal; RAS for the off-diagonal interaction.

evidence.quote: We applied here Watson’s S reduced Hamiltonian in the prolate I$^r$ representation on the diagonal

fitting.value: Test additional reasonable parameters after assignment rounds; retain the parameter improving fit quality most; occasionally test removal of poorly constrained parameters.

evidence.quote: If at least one parameter improved the quality of the fit sufficiently, we chose the one that improved the quality the most and searched for additional parameters.
We tested occasionally if a parameter with relatively large uncertainties can be omitted from the fit without increasing the rms error of the fit by too large amounts.

validation.value: Inspect residuals and blends; total-fit rms 17.3 kHz and rms error 0.839.

evidence.quote: Transitions with modest residuals around three to four times of the experimental uncertainties were marked for occasional inspection.

claims.hypothesis: An extended laboratory analysis can produce sufficiently accurate transition predictions for astronomical searches.
claims.experiment: Measure and assign laboratory rotation-tunneling spectra and fit an expanded spectroscopic Hamiltonian.
claims.result: 11551 transitions at 7551 frequencies; total-fit rms 17.3 kHz and rms error 0.839.
claims.finding: The calculated rotation-tunneling spectrum has sufficient accuracy for radio astronomical searches.

evidence.quote: Our final line list consisted of 11551 transitions from the present study which correspond to 7551 different frequencies, mostly because of unresolved asymmetry splitting.
The rms of 17.3 kHz and the rms error of 0.839 for the total fit are obviously dominated by our data.
The calculated rotation-tunneling spectrum of 3-hydroxypropenal has sufficient accuracy for radio astronomical searches.

claims.hypothesis: The PILS emission is better described by a 125 K excitation temperature than by 300 K.
claims.experiment: Compare the two inherited LTE models against the full PILS survey using improved line frequencies.
claims.result: The 300 K model predicts ~30 undetected lines above 3σ; the 125 K model shows no major issue.
claims.finding: An excitation temperature of 125 K is more appropriate.

evidence.quote: If we check the full survey, no major issue is seen for the model with $T_{\rm ex}$ = 125 K.
Indeed, several undetected lines ($\sim$30) are predicted above 3$\sigma$ with this model
In summary, an excitation temperature of 125 K is more appropriate than 300 K for this species.

claims.hypothesis: Additional archival transitions can confirm 3-hydroxypropenal toward IRAS16293 B.
claims.experiment: Select archival observations, extract spectra at the PILS position, and compare them with the PILS model.
claims.result: Seven additional lines detected at about 3σ or more, with intensities agreeing with the model.
claims.finding: The detection of HOCHCHCHO can be considered secure.

why_this_method.value: Improve uncertain high-excitation frequencies to distinguish the 125 K and 300 K LTE scenarios.

evidence.quote: Based on the previous catalog of 3-hydroxypropenal lines, it was not possible to distinguish between an excitation temperature of 125 K and 300 K for this species.
Indeed, the lines with high $E_{\rm up}$ that should allow us to constrain the excitation temperature, showed too large frequency uncertainties.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Tex = 300 K, N = 1.8 × 10^15 cm−2 does not reproduce the observations.

evidence.quote: However, the model with $T_{\rm ex}$ = 300 K and $N = 1.8 \times 10^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$ does not reproduce the observations.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Lowering the 300 K model column density to 1.0 × 10^15 cm−2 improves agreement but underproduces detected lines.

evidence.quote: A better agreement would be obtained if we lower the column density at $1.0 \times 10^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$.
But several detected lines (Fig. 2 of (cite: 3-HP_det_2022)) are in that case under-produced in terms of intensity.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Exclude obviously blended laboratory lines, with limited exceptions for sufficiently symmetric unresolved or accidental blends.

evidence.quote: Obviously blended lines were in most cases not included in the line list except for unresolved asymmetry doublets and occasionally accidental blends of lines assignable to the ground vibrational state of 3-hydroxypropenal
as long as the line shape was sufficiently symmetric.

limitations_admitted.value: Very few predicted lines in the 300 K calculation up to 1.5 THz have uncertainties exceeding 0.1 MHz and require caution.

evidence.loc: Discussion of the laboratory spectroscopic results
evidence.quote: A calculation at 300 K up to 1.5 THz contains only very few lines with calculated uncertainties exceeding 0.1 MHz; these very few lines should probably be viewed with some caution.

limitations_admitted.value: Residual continuum subtraction problems affect two archival spectral windows.

evidence.loc: Search for additional transitions of 3-hydroxypropenal in the ALMA archive
evidence.quote: We could clearly see that the continuum was not properly subtracted at the extracted position for two spectral windows of the project 2022.1.00554.S (296.4 and 309.7 GHz).

referee_caveats_inferred: The archive-transition table lists 2021.1.01164.S, while the acknowledgements list 2021.1.00544.S; the intended project must be resolved.
The temperature conclusion compares inherited discrete LTE solutions rather than reporting a new temperature likelihood or confidence interval.
Several added detections are near 3σ in a line-rich source; local noise, blending, and the detection statistic need explicit reproduction.
Different archival beams and unspecified beam-filling treatment limit independent intensity comparisons.
The 240.08569 GHz selection footnote associates Eup with units of s−1; the table instead gives Aij = 4.8 × 10−4 s−1, below the nominal search cut.
